Greetings Comrade Liang Renshu.

Before all else, I wish to congratulate you on your recent appointment to the Premiership and wish nothing but the best for your new administration.

I am writing this letter to you today because I had recently returned from my meeting with the Central Committee. I had the greatest joy of meeting with our Comrade and Leader, Cui Fang, with whom we discussed a range of topics that concerned this great nation. For the brevity of this letter, let the depth of our conversation be reserved for another time, when I wish to express with similar joy a recent victory that Qianxun has recently achieved over one of the peoples enemies.

Poverty is the first pestilence of the human race. 

Before all evil is the inability to feed yourself or your family, the circumstances that enables starvation to be practical in saving for a tomorrow. It is the absence of a roof that shelters from the rain, of clothes against the sweltering Sun, the sickness left untreated and the fear of relief that must be paid for with great cost. People say that the root of all evil is greed, but that consigns evil to be an active agent, a culture that affirms fault to be on the actor. But where there must be consequence in exchange for each iniquitous action, it is the duty of the state to alleviate all suffering and to make humans happy.

This is why we practice socialism. It is why we guide the innate greed of the private markets so that a day will rise over Qianxun in which every mouth is cleaned and fed and sleeps soundly in the gentle night for a more prosperous day next. Until the distant time comes in which this world can be enjoined in a communist world, we do we what we must to enrich the revolution for this country.

Poverty is the first enemy, and today Qianxun has eradicated it in its absolute form. Today, by all metrics granted to us by the Science and Technology Committee, the Census Office, the Department of Statistics in the University of Qianxun, third-party observers, and international advisors, there is no absolute poverty in the Qianxun Socialist Republic.

Yesterday, I had the privilege of being the first to receive this news from our dearest Comrade and Leader, who relayed to the Department of Statistics and I of this momentous feat.

Over the course of two decades we observed nearly 38 million of our own citizens escape extreme poverty. In those same two decades we observed a surge in Qianxuns urban population from merely 14 million in 1980 to nearly 54 million in 2024. In 2023, our secondary sector contributed nearly 40% to our national GDP, from what used to just be 15% in 1980. Also in 2024, Qianxun saw 1.9 million individuals from previously impoverished households enter employment and saw per capita disposable income grow by nearly 30% since 2020. 

Since 2025, we have seen the highest number of investments in rural connectivity since the Battle of Danxia, the greatest number of roads, eletrical providers, and internet service providers created for remote villages in nearly a decade, the highest amount of subsidies and infrastructure investments for rural regions in twenty years, the largest-scale census to identify impoverished soviets since 2001, and the greatest expansion to the national healthcare insurance coverage since 2015, and in the next few days Qianxun will have celebrated its very month where not a single citizen had to live below 56 yuan, the official benchmark demarcated by the Census Office for absolute poverty in the country.

This triumph could not have been possible without the ceaseless sacrifice of our dear leaders, of the Min Zhu Party that has been the guiding light for the nations collective conscience, and surely not without the popular masses that have committed to the most exalted task of aiding this socialist republic. 

But victory is not yet complete unless we sustain these gains for the next generation. As we honor this first step, let us not forget that in the arduous journey of the thousand steps, we must speak of a child who will not know of poverty in all of its terrible forms, who will be able to comfortably live within this socialist republic and fear not the possibility that their dreams might be unassailable clouds in a distant sky. 

Though the worst had come to pass, there are still workers in this socialist republic who cannot fulfill the highest extent of their human potential, who live squalidly amidst the cities they have given their lives to prosper and thrive. Until these comrades too are lifted up, our victory remains incomplete. We must now turn our efforts to eradicating relative poverty, so that all may share equally in the fruits of the revolution.

Until then, let us continue to work fortuitously and build a communist society.

Yours,
Dr. Kang Hongxin

In a landmark vote by the House of the Unified Confederacy, the Lamandican parliament has elected [b]Juan Sorobzaul Calieno-Ruiz[/b] as the new prime minister of Lamandica. Raised in a low-income suburb of Wichenvidence, Calieno-Ruiz originally started as an immigration lawyer, but soon turned to politics and eventually became governor of Odrenisus province. The left-leaning candidate vows to preserve Lamandicas civil rights, lower the nations soaring taxes, integration of those struggling in the Tanavaim province, and to open borders and trade to fellow nations of Erene. Though his controversial stance to reinstate prior restrictions of the Llyndorran Virus, he commits to the wellbeing of the nation and working to obtain shipments of vaccines once they are available. At age 44, he is one of the youngest prime ministers in Lamandican history. Nonetheless, until the next Lamandican Prime Minstrel election in five years, Calieno-Ruiz hopes to usher in a new era of prosperity across Lamandica.
